The existence is guaranteed because $\det(A - \lambda I) = 0$ implies the matrix $A - \lambda I$ is singular, meaning its columns are linearly dependent. This singularity ensures the null space (kernel) is non-trivial, so a non-zero vector $v$ must exist such that $(A - \lambda I)v = 0$, which rearranges to $Av = \lambda v$. Since $A - 2I$ is the zero matrix, the null space is the entire $\mathbb{R}^2$, meaning any two linearly independent vectors (like $\mathbf{e}_1$ and $\mathbf{e}_2$) are eigenvectors.
